summary: The five findings from the earlier review are closed by implementation and regression coverage. Two additional P2 contract-validation defects remain: pairing silently removes a leading UTF-8 BOM, and the client overwrites snapshot.events before validating the snapshot response. No P1 findings were identified. All eight registered checks passed at the reviewed source binding.

open_findings.title: Preserve the original JSON text when decoding pairing bodies
open_findings.description: parsePairBody uses TextDecoder without ignoreBOM:true, so a leading UTF-8 BOM is removed before JSON.parse sees the source. A BOM-prefixed otherwise valid pairing object is accepted and consumes its one-time code, contrary to the strict JSON-body contract. The control-body decoder preserves the BOM and rejects it, so the two control paths enforce different grammar.
open_findings.requested_change: Preserve the BOM during pairing-body decoding and let JSON.parse reject it. Add an HTTP regression proving a BOM-prefixed pairing body receives 400 REQUEST_INVALID without consuming the code, followed by successful pairing using the unchanged code.
open_findings.validation_basis: Static source analysis; no reproduction executed.

open_findings.title: Validate the snapshot response before replacing its events
open_findings.description: The client merges the separate events response over snapshot.events before running SyntheticSnapshotSchema.parse. A malformed/missing required snapshot.events field can therefore be accepted whenever /events returns a valid array, bypassing the snapshot wire schema and incorrectly reaching connected rather than recoverable read failure.
open_findings.requested_change: Validate the snapshot response against SyntheticSnapshotSchema before composing the separately validated events response. Add malformed snapshot.events and missing snapshot.events cases while the separate events response remains valid.
open_findings.validation_basis: Static source analysis of the client and required events field in packages/contracts/src/index.ts; no reproduction executed.

previous_findings.evidence: A held-initial-read Chromium regression verifies disconnect aborts and prevents late restore.
Deferred browser tests verify serialization, retained cadence, no overlap, failure persistence and complete recovery.
HTTP tests reject invalid Unicode whitespace, prove no renewal/revoke and accept JSON whitespace.

previous_findings.finding: Originless production-read test used a differently bound capability
previous_findings.evidence: The test pairs for bridge origin and gets 200 without Origin using same-origin metadata.

previous_findings.finding: Restart, WebSocket, denied metadata and server expiry evidence missing
previous_findings.evidence: HTTP restart/upgrade/metadata cases and bridge-clock-driven Chromium AUTH_EXPIRED path pass.

review_boundary: Independent read-only source, contract, configuration and recorded-evidence review. Current source/tests were reviewed; no edits or runtime work by reviewer.
evidence_limits: No files edited and no tests, services or browser sessions started by reviewer.
Passing checks use an injected bridge clock for expiry; they are not elapsed-wall-clock endurance tests.
Static review and synthetic-state checks do not prove OS isolation, all cleanup paths or parent BB-01..10 completion.
Requested model and effort metadata do not attest runtime identity.
